Niczki, yeah. This was like five miles behind the city. It was the woods. And we, for the summer we had there a room and we stayed there short before the holidays and we came back for the holidays. But that summer I remember it was the 30th of August. My mother came and to pick us up much earlier than we were supposed to come, and she says, “It’s terrible things happening in the world and I want you all home, children.” And I was looking at my mother’s gray face, and I asked, “Why? What happened? What happened?” She told me that the war is going on. I said, “War? What can be so bad, the war?” But little did I know.
They marched in on September, ‘39, came out the war. They must have marched in the second or the third day.
